core/landscape/execution/node_states.py:: The handler is the documented Tier-3 quarantine fallback, not a swallow: it assigns input_hash = repr_hash(input_data), so the branch always produces the audit row's input_hash and the insert proceeds. The try runs only under quarantined=True, whose parameter contract (documented on this repository's sibling method record_node_state_open, node_states.py:115-116) states that input_data is Tier-3 external data that may contain non-canonical values (NaN, Infinity) and uses the repr_hash fallback. stable_hash raises exactly ValueError/TypeError on that canonicalization refusal, and repr_hash (src/elspeth/contracts/hashing.py:124-143) exists for precisely this case: its docstring names it the fallback for when canonical_json fails and declares it 'appropriate for Tier-3 (external data) trust boundary where data is already malformed and being quarantined'. R6 fires only because the handler's outcome is an assignment rather than a raise or return. Re-raising is the wrong alternative and would destroy audit evidence rather than protect it: it would refuse to record a node state for a quarantined row, which is the exact row whose evidence the quarantine path exists to preserve. The tuple must also stay narrow -- ValueError/TypeError are the canonicalization refusals; any other fault is a programmer error and still surfaces. The identical already-signed handler at node_states.py:129 (record_node_state_open) is deliberately left untouched and specifically NOT folded together with this one into a shared helper, because extracting the two would shift that site's signed ast_path.
core/landscape/execution_repository.py:R: This is the post-failure idempotency probe, and its contract is confirm-or-defer, not detect-and-report. It runs only inside the outer 'except SQLAlchemyError as exc' unwind (execution_repository.py:1082) and has exactly one success outcome: an exact pre-existing receipt, returned idempotently. Every other outcome -- no receipt row, a state or batch that reads back as None, an unreadable database, or a divergent receipt -- must fall through to the two lines immediately below this handler, which unconditionally raise LandscapePostCommitError or LandscapeRecordError from the original write error. Nothing reaches a caller as success, nothing fails open, and no durable evidence is lost. The AuditIntegrityError arm is not the integrity gate: divergence is detected and reported loudly in-transaction at execution_repository.py:978, where existing_receipt_is_exact raises 'aggregation result receipt retry diverges for batch_id=...' before any insert, pinned by tests/unit/core/landscape/test_aggregation_result_receipt.py::test_completion_failure_rolls_back_node_batch_and_receipt; a divergent receipt is re-reported there on every subsequent attempt. Re-raising or re-classifying inside this handler is the wrong alternative and would regress the audit path: error_type at execution_repository.py:1106 is a caller contract -- LandscapePostCommitError, a LandscapeRecordError subclass, tells the caller the durable write completed -- while AuditIntegrityError derives from bare Exception (src/elspeth/contracts/errors.py:961). Letting it escape here would route a write_body_completed failure past all four LandscapePostCommitError handlers in src/elspeth/engine/executors/state_guard.py (lines 272, 315, 431, 473), whose stated purpose is to avoid double-writing a fallback terminal state on top of an already-persisted terminal transition.
core/landscape/exporter.py:R6:LandscapeE: StopIteration here is the generator return protocol, not an error, and the handler consumes it rather than discarding it: 'bundle = stop.value' binds the AuditExportSpooledBundle that stream_audit_export_bundle_to_spool declares as its return type (src/elspeth/contracts/audit_export.py:1342-1350, Generator[dict[str, ClosedAuditExportJSON], None, AuditExportSpooledBundle]), and the line after the loop yields deep_thaw(bundle.final_manifest) from it -- so the export's final manifest, the hash-chain terminus of the audit bundle, exists only because this handler ran. Catching it is required, not stylistic: export_run is itself a generator (exporter.py:432-436, returning Iterator[dict[str, Any]]), so under PEP 479 a StopIteration escaping this frame would be converted to RuntimeError and destroy the export mid-stream instead of terminating it cleanly. Reading stop.value is also the only way to recover a sub-generator's return value while transforming what it yields: 'for record in stream' and 'next(stream, sentinel)' both discard the return value, and 'yield from' would forward records un-thawed. R6 fires only because the handler's outcome is an assignment plus break rather than a raise or return, and a raise here would abort every successful export. Genuine failures are untouched: any exception from next(stream) other than StopIteration -- including the derivation's own record, byte, and chunk ceiling refusals -- is not caught by this clause and propagates to the caller.
core/landscape/run_coordination_reposito: The caught exception is _ReleaseMembershipMiss, a module-private sentinel (run_coordination_repository.py:112) raised at exactly one site -- this method's own body at line 622 -- and caught at exactly one site, here. It is Tier-1 internal control flow: it carries no external cause, never escapes this module, and is not an error being discarded. The rollback is its entire purpose: begin_write commits on successful block exit and rolls back on exception (src/elspeth/core/landscape/database.py:245-246), so a bare 'return' at line 622 would COMMIT the seat clear without the matching run_workers departure and without the leader_release coordination event, splitting the one atomic transition the docstring promises into a half-applied state. Raising the sentinel is the only way to roll all three back; catching it here converts that rollback into the documented no-op. R6 fires solely because the handler's bare 'return' yields None, which the rule's _is_default_return_value heuristic classes as a silent default -- but release_seat is typed '-> None' and returns None on every path, so None is the method's whole signature, not a swallowed outcome. Re-raising is the wrong alternative: release_seat is graceful-shutdown hygiene, explicitly idempotent, and its documented contract already makes a rowcount-0 seat CAS (already released, or deposed) a silent no-op, so crashing teardown because a worker row was already departed would turn benign shutdown ordering into a fatal error while the seat lease still expires on its own heartbeat. No audit evidence is lost: the transaction rolled back zero-mutation, so there is nothing left to explain.
